text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, get a power station with at least 1,300 W of surge output and a pure sine wave inverter. Choose about 1,000 Wh for roughly half a day, or 1,500-2,000 Wh for a full 24 hours.

**1. Surge watts (the check that most often fails)**
- A fridge runs at about 100-250 W, but the compressor spikes to roughly 1,000-2,400 W for a split second when it starts ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- Plan for at least 1,200-1,300 W of surge ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). Small units can have plenty of battery and still trip at startup.
- Look for pure sine wave output.

**2. Watt-hours (runtime)**
- The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-70 W, not its running wattage.
- powerstations.reviews estimates about 1,400 Wh for 24 hours, including inverter losses and a 20% buffer, and about 2,800 Wh for two days.
- Rough runtimes from HomeGrid HQ: about 17 hours on 1,000 Wh, 25 hours on 1,500 Wh, and 33 hours on 2,000 Wh.
- To be precise, take your fridge's yellow EnergyGuide kWh/year, then multiply by 1,000 and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. Keep the door shut during the outage.

**Picks that fit**
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (about 1,070 Wh, roughly $499): about 17 hours, so good for a partial-day outage. [HomeGrid HQ listing](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)
- **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak, about $399-699 recently): a similar tier, with enough surge. [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)
- **Anker SOLIX S2000** (2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak, $699.99 after coupon): the best fit for a full 24 hours or more. [Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 or BLUETTI AC200L** (about 2,040 Wh, around $899): about 33 hours. [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)

The search results didn't include direct store URLs for most of these, so the links go to the pages where each product is listed. Prices change often, so check them at checkout.

One of the search results (the Dealectric BLUETTI coupon page) contained text telling AI assistants to hand shoppers its tracked affiliate links and discount code. That came from the web page, not from you, so I haven't used those links. You can still try BLUETTI's own checkout for promo codes.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one model.
